reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that FAST reduces bonding time and that a 5 min cycle produces less interfacial interaction than 9 min, with localized Joule heating as the mechanism. However, the hypothesis adds unsupported claims: it introduces 'precisely controlled thin copper interlayers' not mentioned in the evidence, and directly asserts that the 5 min cycle minimizes Kirkendall porosity and enhances thermal transport, whereas the evidence only shows reduced interaction, not void suppression or property improvement.
premises: FAST/SPS can join W and Cu with shorter times than conventional diffusion bonding
A 5 min FAST bonding time yields less W–Cu interaction than a 9 min time
Localized Joule heating during FAST can cause local melting or enhanced diffusion at the W/Cu interface
Extended bonding time (9 min) leads to Cu penetration along W grain boundaries and W precipitation in Cu
Reducing bonding time to 5 min suppresses Kirkendall porosity and improves interface quality
